tasks.title: Optimize mul_mat_q (MMQ) kernel (high potential). NOTE: mmq for SYCL is not enabled by default, need to change ggml_sycl_supports_mmq to enable it.
tasks.outcome_notes: MMQ is disabled by default (accuracy issues). Enabled it for 7 types with QI<=WARP_SIZE=16, implemented _INTEL macros (WG=256), added reqd_sub_group_size. Benchmarks show MMQ is 2.2x slower than MMVQ/DMMV (n<=8) and 1.6x slower than oneMKL (n=512). Accuracy failure: q4_0 n=512 ERR=0.999572. Reverted ggml_sycl_supports_mmq to return false. mmq.cpp improvements kept dormant. Only joint_matrix/XMX (opt_001_008) could make MMQ competitive. Steps opt_001_003-007 skipped.

steps.notes: Implemented _INTEL macros with nwarps=16 (WG=256) for all 10 quant formats. Added reqd_sub_group_size(WARP_SIZE) to all 20 launch sites. However, benchmarking with FORCE_MMQ showed MMQ is ~2.2x slower than MMVQ/DMMV for n=1..8, and ~1.6x slower than oneMKL for n=512. Also has accuracy issues (q4_0 n=512 ERR=0.999572). The original devs disabled MMQ entirely (returns false for all types) with TODO about accuracy issues. ggml_sycl_supports_mmq change reverted. mmq.cpp kernel improvements kept as dormant code. MMQ is fundamentally not competitive on Xe2/SIMD16 — it needs dp4a/joint_matrix to be useful. Remaining MMQ optimization steps (opt_001_003 through opt_001_007) are BLOCKED until the accuracy issue is resolved and MMQ becomes competitive. Only opt_001_008 (joint_matrix/XMX) could make MMQ worthwhile.

steps.notes: Implemented SLM caching (cooperative Y-vector load into local_accessor<block_q8_1>) with use_slm template parameter and MMVQ_SLM_Y_LIMIT=48KB budget check in all 11 multicol launchers. tasks.title: Optimize vecdotq kernel (medium potential)
tasks.progress_notes: All steps evaluated and skipped. Analysis: (1) opt_008_001 DPCT cleanup — massive refactoring (53 dp4a + 21 vectorized_binary + 5 byte_level_permute) for 0-5% gain, high risk of breaking critical quantized inference. (2) opt_008_002 aligned loads — non-aligned helpers exist for genuinely unaligned data, unclear benefit.
